title: Iliotibial Band Syndrome
claims: Johns Hopkins describes IT band syndrome as pain on the outside of the knee, commonly in distance runners, with aching or burning that may spread up the thigh to the hip.

Johns Hopkins notes pain tends to be worst immediately after foot strike, may begin near the end of a workout, and as the condition worsens starts earlier and persists after exercise; stairs may worsen it.
Johns Hopkins lists uneven or downhill terrain, worn-out shoes, high daily mileage, and bowlegged alignment as risk factors.
Johns Hopkins states the exact cause is still debated, but repetitive bending and extending of the knee is clearly involved.
Johns Hopkins says most people respond to conservative treatment and surgery is considered only after 6 months of other therapies.
Johns Hopkins prevention advice includes running on even surfaces, replacing shoes, easing training, alternating track directions, and stretching the outer thigh and hamstrings.
